blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Philippine nickel producers expect production to remain relatively unchanged this year, as erratic weather conditions and subdued global prices continue to impact the country’s mining industry. Philippine Nickel Industry Association (PNIA) president Dante Bravo said the sector is unlikely to see a significant increase in output in 2026, partly because unpredictable rainfall is disrupting mining activities. READ: Nickel Asia seals $30-M Kazakhstan deal In 2025, the volume of nickel ore meant for direct shipping rose 5.6 percent to 37.81 million dry metric tons (DMT), while the value of nickel ore output fell 18.1 percent to P69.36 billion.
